editorial:
Imagine a small, sad group of neo-Nazis trying to make a name for themselves in a big city. They are not scary; they are actually kind of pathetic. You will meet a young leader who is way in over his head and lacks any real confidence. Everything changes when a mysterious man shows up and starts pulling the strings. He tells the group exactly how to gain power and get noticed, turning these losers into something much more dangerous. The vibe is tense and weird, making you wonder who this strange mentor really is and what he actually wants from these people.

What really works here is how the movie builds a sense of dread. The acting is solid, especially as you watch the young leader slowly lose his mind. While some parts feel a bit slow, the big reveal at the end makes the wait worth it. If you enjoy old-school thrillers with a twist, you should definitely check this out. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend night.
endingExplained: The big twist is that the mysterious mentor is actually the ghost or spirit of Adolf Hitler. He has been manipulating the young leader from the shadows to try and bring his hateful ideas back to life. In the final scenes, the truth comes out, but it does not lead to a grand victory. Instead, the plan falls apart, showing that hate only leads to failure. The movie ends by proving that the old evil cannot truly return.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old mystery thrillers and psychological twists.
